requirements.evidence: All contract members are present: Queues properties/methods and view data `accessQueue`/`accessGrants` (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:24-261, render at :211-226). Serve has `selectedQueueId` set on mount to the first callable queue, `mode` validated `in:any,priority_only,normal_only`, `#[Locked] lastCalledTicketId`, and `callNext()` with the required exception-to-notice mapping, an uncaught AuthorizationException, and a rate limiter hit only on success (Serve.php:49-97). The waiting list is ordered priority desc, issued_at, id, filtered by mode and limited to 30 (Serve.php:130-158). Routes are at routes/web.php:59-60. Members tabs with `role="tablist"`, `setActiveTab` whitelist, and the invite form/pending invites only on the invites tab are in members.blade.php:6-95 and Members.php:68-73. Navbar entries are gated by `create` Queue / `view` entity (default-page.blade.php:49-56). Every listed lang key exists in both locales. Rename re-derives the slug (`slug: Str::slug(trim($this->renameName))`, Queues.php:140). Toggle uses an in-page modal, not wire:confirm (queues.blade.php:100-123).

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through CreateQueue/UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess/CallNextTicket. `#[Validate]` + `validateOnly` are used for `name`, `renameName` and `mode`. Ids are resolved via `$this->entity->queues()->findOrFail()` and `memberships()->findOrFail()`. CHANGELOG and docs/business-rules.md are updated. Deviations: `toggleActive`, `grantAccess` and `revokeAccess` have no `$this->authorize(...)` in the component and rely only on the action's internal check (Queues.php:168-175, 238-244), which the Livewire policy rule 3 requires. Four modals repeat the same modal-card markup instead of a Blade component (queues.blade.php:31-165). `setActiveTab` has no PHPDoc (Members.php:68).

security.evidence: Every client id is resolved scoped to the entity (Queues.php:103, 117, 133, 170, 179, 240-241; Serve.php:73, 135). render uses `find` scoped to the entity, so a tampered `viewingQueueId`/`accessQueueId` discloses nothing (Queues.php:213-221). `lastCalledTicketId` is `#[Locked]` and `callNext` is rate-limited (Serve.php:43-44, 75-79). Output uses `{{ }}` throughout, with no `{!! !!}`. Remaining gap: the toggle/grant/revoke endpoints have no component-level authorize. The risk is limited because the actions authorize internally and ids are entity-scoped.

tests.evidence: QueuesPageTest.php and ServePanelTest.php cover the happy paths, validation and duplicate-slug errors, slug re-derivation, the toggle modal without wire:confirm, grant/revoke with the audit log, foreign-id not-found for each id-taking method (dataset at QueuesPageTest.php:~300-307), tampered accessQueueId/viewingQueueId, the locked `lastCalledTicketId`, the rate limit, mode filtering, the 30-ticket cap, the no-grant 403 for callNext, and navbar visibility per role. Gaps: the only unauthorized-call test in Queues is for `create`; rename/toggleActive/grantAccess/revokeAccess are never called by an employee. The pt_BR members locale test dropped `->assertDontSee('Invite member', false)` (MembersTest.php:~404), which slightly weakens an existing assertion.

simplicity.evidence: Components are direct and reuse domain actions and policies (`$user->can('call', $queue)` in Serve.php:120). No extra layers were added. Bulma modal shells are duplicated four times in queues.blade.php instead of an anonymous `<x-modal>` component. `accessGrants` filters in PHP after loading all QueueAccess rows (Queues.php:233-237), which is acceptable.

readability.evidence: Names are clear, methods are short, and docblocks explain the untrusted-state properties (Queues.php:36-58). Minor style issues: modal markup is mis-indented (`<div class="modal-card mx-3">` is nested deeper than its siblings, queues.blade.php:34-53). The navbar serve link lacks the indentation used by sibling `@can` blocks (default-page.blade.php:54-55). `firstMessage` has an odd fallback `__('validation.required', ['attribute' => 'name'])` (Queues.php:259).

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: the two components and views, routes, navbar, lang keys, members tabs, docs/CHANGELOG, and tests. The extra lang keys (e.g. `serve_rate_limited`, `queues_reactivate`) support required features. Existing tests were changed only where the tab split required it (EntityInviteTest.php:179-184, MembersTest.php).

issues.explanation: `toggleActive`, `grantAccess` and `revokeAccess` call no `$this->authorize(...)` in the component and rely only on the domain action's internal check, so they do not follow the Livewire policy rule that every public action authorizes server-side.

Only `create` has an unauthorized-call test; no test shows that an employee calling rename, toggleActive, grantAccess or revokeAccess directly is denied, although the conventions require one per action.
The pt_BR locale test lost its `assertDontSee('Invite member', false)` check when the assertions moved behind `setActiveTab('invites')`, which slightly weakens an existing test.
The Bulma modal shell (background, card, head with close button, foot) is copy-pasted four times instead of being extracted into an anonymous Blade component, as the conventions ask.
The modal-card blocks are indented one level deeper than their sibling `.modal-background`, so the closing `` structure is hard to follow.
The serve navbar link is not indented inside its `@can` block, unlike the neighbouring entries.
The new public method `setActiveTab` has no PHPDoc; the conventions ask for PHPDoc on public methods that were touched.
The fallback message in `firstMessage` hardcodes a `validation.required` text for attribute 'name', even when it is used for `renameName` errors.

review.summary: The change adds the Queues management page and the Serve panel as Livewire components on top of the existing domain actions, splits the Members page into tabs, adds navbar links and both locales, updates the docs and ships extensive Pest tests. Requirements, entity scoping of every client id, tamper handling and rate limiting are done well. The main reservations are missing component-level authorize calls (and matching unauthorized-call tests) on toggle/grant/revoke, duplicated modal markup, and small style nits, so I would approve with follow-up nits.
